notes: Summary: small dev tools startup building a VS Code extension (Codex Loom) that provides streaming inline completions and per-line suggestions.
Primary ask: sub-100ms incremental update for streaming completion, ability to pin model versions per-customer and quick rollback, quotas and per-dev rate limits for extension users.
Customer quote (CTO): 'We need the editor to feel instantaneous — if completion lags our retention drops.'
Architecture preference: hosted inference for fast time-to-market, but dedicated pools for larger enterprise customers. Interested in private/VPC for select customers later.
Security: SSO (SAML) must be supported, audit logs retained 1 year, keys via customer KMS, and option for EU data residency for EU customers.
Cost sensitivity: high for free-tier users — looking for aggressive batching/caching recommendations; willing to pay for dedicated capacity for big enterprise deals.

Integration notes: wants streaming over websocket from Redwood -> VS Code extension, fallback to short LSP calls when offline. Concern about rate limiting for open-source contributors — needs token throttling per-extension-install.
Internal contacts: CTO Maya Chen, Head of Product Liam O'Rourke, Lead Engineer Priya Nandakumar.
Sales notes: offered 90-day POC (50k tokens/day cap), sent pricing deck + security FAQ. Drive deck link above.
SE feedback (Marco): initial latency tests good on GPU-backed variant, prefix caching could reduce cost by ~30% for typical dev sessions.
Quote from dev during demo: 'Inline completions look clean, but the cursor jitter at 80ms needs smoothing — consider token-buffering.'
Procurement: legal requested data processing addendum and SOC2 attestation; security has open question about retention controls for telemetry.
Next demo scheduled: 2026-03-18 with eng + security to run SAML flow and simulated high-concurrency of 800 active devs.
POC milestones: (1) streaming latency baseline, (2) model pin/rollback test, (3) rate-limit behavior under extension churn, (4) SAML SSO end-to-end.
Notes style: shorthand, action items mixed in — see timeline for recent activity.
